rounds.report:
Representation level: L1 (proxy). CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline, native round 2.

Observed in the 24 reference samples: one continuous star-tracker time-lapse over a crater lake, with no cuts. The Milky Way, Jupiter and Saturn, and a reddish star stay fixed in frame. The landscape rolls counter-clockwise (horizon about -16 deg at 0 s, about level near 6 s, about +32 deg at 18.6 s) and slides left. The landscape consists of the far crater rim, the lake with a dark cinder island, the near rim and cliff with shoreline snow on the right, left-foreground conifers, rocks and a dead snag (out of frame after about 10 s), and crest conifers at upper right after about 13 s. The sky goes from twilight with lake mist, to dark teal with yellow light domes and airglow, to brighter cyan. Short light events occur at about 1.7 s (blue lamp), 5.07 s (red light on the foreground tree and snag), and 13.5 s and 16.9 s (red car lights). The clip fades to black from about 18.6 s to 19.4 s.

Camera and timing: one fixed-position perspective camera rotates about the celestial polar axis (latitude 43 deg). The hour angle is linear in time (-20.4 deg + 3.707 deg/s), with pitch 13.3 deg and roll 2.7 deg at hour angle 0, and a vertical FOV of about 71.4 deg. I fitted these to hand-measured landmark tracks and horizon tilts from the reference samples, with an RMS of about 5 px at 960x540. The sky group shares the tracker rotation, so it stays fixed in frame. Time is absolute (frame/30) over 583 frames.

Geometry: a far-rim wall strip on the measured skyline. Near-rim/cliff and left-foreground ground surfaces built from measured crest and shore outlines in azimuth/elevation. The lake is a polar grid whose colours include the mirrored sky and glow, so the reflection moves correctly. The island is a flattened half-ellipsoid, trees are cones on trunks, the snag is a leaning thin cylinder, and snow patches are small quads. Transient lights are additive points, and the fade is a black camera-attached plane.

Render feedback received (round 1 render, all 24 pairs inspected): camera motion, horizon roll, sky placement and terrain layout matched closely. The renderer evidently applies filmic tone mapping, which crushed darks and over-saturated mid-tones. Round 2 revisions:
- Tone mapping is disabled per material, so colours are reproduced directly.
- Sky, terrain, lake and glow colours are recalibrated from region averages measured on the reference samples.
- The Milky Way is redrawn as a narrower, mottled band with a reddish side lobe, on a denser sky mesh, with more stars.
- The green airglow is weaker and the yellow light domes stronger.
- The lake is darker and more reflective.
- Foreground rocks are much darker.
- The island is shallower, so it no longer looks too tall in frame.
- The snag lean now follows its observed top and base.

Inference and remaining uncertainty: motion between samples is assumed to be constant-rate rotation. Off-frame crest and terrain are extrapolated. Distances cannot be observed under pure rotation, so they are chosen to be plausible. Light-event durations are guesses. The fine shape of the Milky Way, the star density and the terrain texture are deliberately simplified for L1. None of the round-2 changes has been verified by a render yet.
